item: The engine's failure lines are scrubbed where the P0 verify check copies them, an empty secret matches nothing in cut text, and the passphrase guard reads the release run's own modules and says exactly where it stops
key_paths: src/monitoring/p0_validation.py; src/monitoring/secret_scrub.py; tests/test_p0_validation.py; tests/test_secret_scrub.py; docs/CHANGES.md; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md; docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md; docs/ledger/SHIPPED_LOG.md
summary: The coordinator's delta check of #1312 (verdict: nits) found one route of the shape of the passphrase finding that no handler-based test reaches (F2): verify_stream_backup returns its failure lines as data (problems), a decrypt failure's line carries the exception's own words, and the verify check copies the list into its measurements (the P0 file the debug bundle carries) and its reason (a release run's state and report). Every message the engine raises there is a literal today, so nothing leaked; the lines are now scrubbed line by line where the check copies them, never the verdict or the check's own words around them (the run puts no minimum on a passphrase's length). Tests: a distinctive passphrase is absent from the result and the written file with the engine's own list left unedited, and a passphrase of pass or fail leaves the verdict and the lead of the reason alone; five mutations are each caught. F3: _scrub_cut_text with an empty secret raised empty separator since the rewrite and returns the text again (unreachable through scrub_file, which returns earlier), one assertion and one mutation. F1: the ledger said the static test makes a fifth handler impossible to add unseen; it held the handlers of the functions of p0_validation.py that take a parameter named passphrase, and the first fix said so. The coordinator's delta check then listed twelve ways a caught exception can reach a text, of which the test saw seven, and asked for release_run.py to be read too. The test now holds the handlers of every function that holds the passphrase (a parameter, a local or an attribute named passphrase, or a secret or needle) in p0_validation.py, release_run.py and the restore child, to using the caught exception only inside a call that scrubs it with the secret (_exception_text, _error_text, scrub_value, _log_phase_failure, the secret at the position each reads it), as its class, or as a phase error's status and partial. Read with that rule, release_run.py has no handler that writes an unscrubbed message: the walk flagged four uses in two handlers, all forms the first walk had no word for (the class name in a log line, a phase error's status and partial), and its scrubs are not the p0 helper, so the accepted routes are a table in the test, each pinned both ways. What stays outside it is stated in LESSONS, the shipped log and the shipped row: a secret held as **kwargs, a pw or a closure (the job worker's two online probes put the text of a network call into their result and are handed no secret), a helper that reads the exception for itself, a bare re-raise, a raise without from, a finally, an alias of the traceback module, repr(locals()), the engine's lines handed back as data, and any other module. The walk's own tests grew from twenty-three to forty-seven (a handler named err, the exception as a helper's second argument, an empty or missing or other secret, the secret at another position, the secret off the run's parameters, a local, secret and needle) and forty mutations of the walk are each caught, including the two the check found alive (the handler name hard-coded as exc, and the exception accepted at any position). Lesson: LESSONS.md, the entry on the passphrase in what the P0 phase catches.
